answer: Cross-epoch action fingerprint: each identity’s signed actions are hashed per epoch, and next-epoch admission requires 70% similarity with its prior profile, including yarrow task cadence. An attacker must sustain consistent histories across epochs or pay a fresh 14-day, 200-action observation window before its interaction vertex is trusted. Juniper-class peers sample histories, so mass identity churn is throttled by per-identity review and missed-opportunity cost.
